hook: The king of six wives, who broke with Rome to found the Church of England.

pages.x: Henry was born in 1491, the second son of Henry VII, the first Tudor king. When his elder brother Arthur died, he became heir, and in 1509, at 17, king: tall, athletic, a fine dancer and musician. He married Arthur's widow, Catherine of Aragon.

Henry wrote music and poetry. This song is his: "Pastime with good company, I love and shall until I die." The tune Greensleeves is often said to be his too, but probably is not. He also loved jousting, wrestling and real tennis.

Catherine gave him a daughter, Mary, but no son who lived. Henry fell in love with Anne Boleyn and asked the pope to end his marriage. The pope, under the thumb of Catherine's nephew, the emperor Charles V, refused.

So Henry broke with the Catholic Church. In 1534 Parliament made him Supreme Head of the Church of England. He closed the monasteries and seized their lands. Those who refused to accept him, like his old chancellor Thomas More, were beheaded.
"Divorced, beheaded, died; divorced, beheaded, survived," English children chant. Anne Boleyn and Catherine Howard lost their heads; Jane Seymour gave him his son, Edward, and died soon after.

He built up the Royal Navy with great warships. In 1545 he watched his favourite, the Mary Rose, heel over and sink off Portsmouth with most of her crew. Her hull was raised from the seabed in 1982 and is now a museum.
A jousting accident left him with an ulcer on his leg that never healed. He grew enormous and bad-tempered, and died in 1547.
Henry VIII broke England away from the Catholic Church and founded the Church of England, which still has the monarch at its head. His six marriages made him the most famous of all English kings.
